newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: Strong foreign buying and futures-driven trade hoisted South African shares to new highs, pushing the all-share index above the 7,600 level for the first time in big turnover trade led by fuels firm Sasol.

Dealers said the weaker rand, which tumbled to its lowest level in seven months, drew offshore interest as shares became cheaper for overseas investors. Rand hedges and gold stocks also gained on some local concerns about the currency.
Futures-related basket trades and asset swaps, one of which took place in Sasol, also drove the market to turnover of around 1.9 billion rand -- more than double an average day's takings.
"There's been lots of basket futures activity, asset swaps and foreign involvement. The futures guys were especially busy covering short positions after yesterday's gains," a dealer said.
Stronger world markets where the U.K's FTSE rose to new highs after an interest rate hike there and a stronger start on Wall Street added momentum to the local market.
Expectations of a local interest rate cut was a further drawcard for investors, dealers said.

Sasol added 75 cents to 59 rand in turnover of almost 300 million rand's worth of shares helping to raise the industrial index by 67.1 points to a new closing high of 9,314.2. The industrial near-month futures contract was last at 8,759/65 from 8,745 settlement.

Major participation in some of the biggest deals by broking firms Merrill Lynch Smith Borkum Hare and SBC Warburg lead to market speculation that the companies were involved in a possible structured product deal.
SBC in June executed a two billion rand offshore portfolio trade for fund manager Southern Asset Management.

Benchmark stock De Beers jumped over five percent to a new 178 rand high in active futures-related trade, pushing the all share index to add 67.6 points to a fresh closing peak of 9,314.2, dealers said.
September all-share futures were last at 6,775/84 from 6,746.
Advancing issues led decliners by 252 to 135.
Clothing retailer Pep slipped 75 cents to 31.50 rand after setting a new 1997 high earlier in active bookover dealings of over six million shares.
Gold shares were overshadowed by positive activity on the gold board, adding 10.1 points to close at 967.1.
